prompt: I've been accused of sending "buongiornissimo"-like messages, but I don't know what that means
response: "Buongiornissimo" is an exaggerated way of saying "good morning" in Italian, emphasizing a very cheerful or overly familiar greeting. If you're not intentionally trying to be overly familiar, you might want to stick to more standard greetings to avoid any misunderstandings.
